recG4mC1e79KaK37p.Bio: Jason Quitt is a Canadian author and researcher of ancient mysticism, sacred geometry and archaeo-astronomy, and the founder of The Crystal Sun. A graduate of the Institute of Energy Wellness who has studied energy modalities, shamanism and Qi Gong since 2002, he has taught and lectured on mysticism, meditation and out of body experience since 2010. His books include Egyptian Postures of Power, The Yosef Codes, Astral Genesis, Gates of the Anunnaki and Astral Experiences. His latest, The Shining Island: Precession, Axis Mundi, & Plato's Celestial Allegory, reads Plato's Atlantis not as a sunken empire but as a celestial allegory encoding the fall of the pole star and the precession of the Great Year.
recG4mC1e79KaK37p.Name: Jason Quitt
recG4mC1e79KaK37p.Role: Author & researcher of ancient mysticism, sacred geometry & archaeo-astronomy

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The Two Mounds Motif, Traced Around the World", "body": "The spine of the night is a single image: a sun cradled between two peaks. Quitt walks it from a roughly thousand year old Fremont pictograph in Utah, which McHugh has photographed filling with sunlight at 6:21 on the summer solstice, to a thirteen mound solar calendar in Peru, a Swedish petroglyph dated near 700 BC, the Egyptian akhet hieroglyph with its paired Aker lions, a Mayan Kukulkan glyph, and Mesopotamian seals showing Enki rising between mounds of creation. Quitt contends the meaning stays fixed across all of them, marking horizon, harvest, death in the west and rebirth in the east."}, {"title": "Crowns Measured in Degrees", "body": "Quitt's central claim is that ancient headdresses are instruments, not decoration. Overlaying protractor lines on Moche goldwork from Peru, he argues the crowns resolve to 23.5 degrees for the tilt of the earth, plus 28.5 and 18.5 degrees for the extremes reached by the moon over its 18.6 year cycle. He runs the same measurement on huge bronze masks from an unnamed ancient Chinese culture, finding 45 degree squares at the eyes and 28.5 degrees within them, and then on McHugh's Utah oar headed figure, whose hat, body and arm protrusions he reports at the same values. Chance asks the obvious question: did they have protractors?"}, {"title": "Diffusion Versus Parallel Invention", "body": "McHugh frames the real dispute plainly, saying most academics hold that these correspondences arose independently rather than through contact. Quitt pushes the other way, noting Utah and coastal Peru sit roughly 9,000 miles apart, a walk of some 750 days at twelve miles a day, yet the Fremont and Moche overlapped in time and imagery. McHugh points to the Harvard oceanographer Barry Fell, who reported foreign scripts scratched into rocks along the Baja coast, and to Christine Pellech's migration and diffusion site. Chance adds that Etruscan filigree may be the only comparable goldwork, and complains that too many key artifacts sit in private collections."}, {"title": "Reading the Sky From Utah Rock", "body": "McHugh's own slides move from Barrier Canyon style panels he dates roughly 2000 BC to 400 or 500 AD, made by hunter gatherers whose life he calls an extended camping trip, into the agricultural Fremont with their one rod and bundle basketry and their horned dancers. He identifies warrior twin figures as Venus, morning and evening star, and shows Chimney Rock in Colorado, where he says Pueblos were built in nineteen year increments to witness the major lunar standstill then underway. A half dollar sized rhyolite pendant carries thirteen circles for thirteen moons; Slick Dissident counts nineteen notches, matching the metonic cycle of 235 lunations."}, {"title": "Severed Heads, Split Bodies and the Squared Field", "body": "Both men read decapitation imagery as harvest code rather than mere violence. McHugh describes Fremont figures carrying staff, obsidian blade and head, and the Dresden Codex maize god as a severed head sprouting corn; Quitt links it to Egyptian material and to a decapitated figure on pillar 43 at Gobekli Tepe, tying it to the autumn equinox. Chance widens it to creation by dismemberment, from Marduk and Tiamat to Quetzalcoatl, Pan Gu's egg and the Norse Ymir. McHugh closes on the Pegasus square, which he identifies with the Iku field, the garden of Eden, Noah's ark and the squared Jerusalem of Revelation."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Tonight's stream will be a rare treat, with the first time on-screen meeting of Archeo-Astronomer John McHugh and sacred geometry mystery seeker Jason Quitt. These two authors have both made incredible discoveries about the ancient world and the astrotheological systems implicit in mythology & religious artifacts. You'll never look at the scripture in the stars the same way after this episode!
